historical_context.time_period: Kalsa's standing present, during the preparation for the reopened Ash-Halo Court armament; absolute date remains unresolved.
historical_context.location: The fixture-bounded tributary bakehouse at Ninth Furnace, immediately below one controlled stair and slatted threshold leading toward the Ash-Halo furnace court.
historical_context.summary: The Ash-Below Compact conducts ordinary bread and relief accounting before Ninth Furnace's registrar exposes its copy route. Ves must decide whether to complete three separate claims, provision affected households, turn exposure into lawful leverage, or preserve an outer copy before the second horn.

public_facts.text: Jamnai branch institutions allocate protection while technical stewards retain control of dangerous heatwork operation.
The earlier Ash-Halo armament drew protection from outer shrines, crossed a mortuary route, and left familiar presences silent after its answer roll remained sealed.
Answer rolls record familiar signs and witnesses around great rites without proving the identity or intention of a manifestation.
Ninth Furnace's present armament offers one recognized-share petition before the divine route opens and has withdrawn ordinary protection from a hostel and furnace-family shrine.

ambient_pressures.text: A divine faction acts through mortal registrars, stewards, intermediaries, champions, stores, and admission tokens, none of which individually owns the god or the dead.

The Ash-Below Compact's strength comes from split custody and constituencies: branch exposure reveals its members but cannot remove the hostel, bakehouse, shrine, and mortuary work Ninth Furnace still needs.
Ash Hook can benefit from delay at Ninth Furnace, but its missing fracture copy and the legitimacy of its diversion remain unresolved; the fixture must not make it the compact's secret owner.
Concentrated divine work is vulnerable to rival intervention and hungry dead, but no participant can infer full metaphysical identity from radiance, silence, or a familiar sign.

groups.label: Ash-Below Compact
institutional_logic: Coordinate covenant petition, potential withdrawal, mortuary evidence, and material relief while keeping their offices separate.
material_incentives: Feed households whose protection was withdrawn
Prevent one registrar from owning the only history
internal_virtues: Ambition cut before dependants are cut
internal_shames: A carrier sold for a cleaner hearing
A relief list that excludes inconvenient households
A familiar name used to hide a dangerous feeder
prestige_markers: A store opened before hunger decides the appeal
A refusal recorded in more than one jurisdiction
taboo_triggers: One member claiming to speak for the dead
A branch calling coordinated lawful offices a private army
A patron purchasing the fallback route
emotional_display_norms: Fear is compressed into inventory work, custody jokes, route marks, and arguments over who is still owed.
trust_defaults: Trusts divided records and material support more than divine certainty; trusts members only within their named office and next handoff.

groups.label: Ninth Furnace continuity faction
institutional_logic: Open the Iron Shelter's armament route before Ash Hook consolidates the East Collar gate.
material_incentives: Restore heat to the hostel and bakehouse
internal_virtues: A champion who reaches the gate before the opening closes
internal_shames: A branch delayed by subordinate paperwork
A rite feeding an unrecognized claimant
A victory that cannot restore its withdrawn shrines
prestige_markers: An armament completed on the forecasted interval
A refusal entered as contained dissent
taboo_triggers: Independent carriers entering a divine route
emotional_display_norms: Urgency is expressed as admission control, clean rosters, horn timing, and contempt for procedural multiplication.
trust_defaults: Trusts recognized branch offices and witnesses inside the docket; treats unlisted coordination as rival command.

groups.label: Hostel, shrine, and tributary bakehouse households
institutional_logic: Keep food, heat, burial testimony, and household standing through a divine allocation made elsewhere.
material_incentives: Receive marked bread and lamp oil
internal_shames: A household protected by another household's erasure
A hidden reserve captured by a new patron
prestige_markers: A receipt the branch must recognize
A full tray when the shrine goes quiet
taboo_triggers: Being reduced to a withdrawal line
The gate war used to erase ordinary claims
emotional_display_norms: Political alignment is expressed through queues, work attendance, answered marks, and who carries food to an absent household.
trust_defaults: Trusts whoever delivers the promised material support; remains divided over gods, sects, and branch loyalty.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The compact must coordinate several lawful authorities closely enough to bite while keeping any one arrest or seizure from owning the whole claim.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Give Ves choices that strengthen copies, relief, solidarity, public standing, or fallback routes at different costs; no choice may grant control of divine identity or the court machinery.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: The branch gains speed and security by forcing several claims through one admission token, but that compression gives the registrar political ownership over which problem exists.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Nema should enforce a plausible branch boundary and preserve exact records while interpreting every ambiguity in Ninth Furnace's favor.

cultural_pressure_fields.summary: A later appeal is meaningless if withdrawn households run out of food, lamp fuel, heat, or witness support first.
cultural_pressure_fields.projection_use: Make every record strategy answer the immediate distribution line and every relief strategy preserve who remains owed.

observer_read: A rival branch hidden inside mortuary procedure
target_self_read: Several bounded offices making one divine refusal reviewable
A relief network that remains useful after exposure
misread_patterns: Treats a copied sign as a claimed identity
Treats every delay beneficiary as the plot's owner
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Let Nema identify real security risks without turning her suspicion into proof of Ash Hook control or hostile dead identity.

observer_read: A divine faction using one token to own three jurisdictions
A branch willing to spend outer shrines for a visible champion
target_self_read: The only organized protection capable of retaking the East Collar gate before the forecasted opening closes
misread_patterns: Can reduce real siege pressure to patron ambition
Can assume every clean docket is deliberate concealment rather than hurried control
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Keep the compact wary of concentrated power while making the material cost of delay and a failed gate assault legible.

observer_read: People who may preserve a perfect case and deliver cold bread
Useful storekeepers mixed with sect business
target_self_read: The network keeping food and appeal alive together
misread_patterns: Can judge secrecy by immediate distribution only
Can treat a route sacrificed for later evidence as abandonment
factional_misread_matrix.projection_use: Ensure household reactions follow material support and visibility rather than automatic loyalty to the compact.

role_pressure_fields.summary: A local clerk whose marks connect ordinary food distribution to branch promises and copied evidence.
obligations: Separate office list from route list
Do not turn accounting into divine testimony
failure_modes: Preserving evidence while households go hungry

role_pressure_fields.summary: A Ninth Furnace record officer who controls branch admission and preserves exact refusals while interpreting them for the holder.
obligations: Protect the rite from unlisted routes
Record decisions the branch may later need
failure_modes: Making one bearer own several jurisdictions
Preserving a record so partisan that rival copies become stronger

role_pressure_fields.summary: A public claimant who can recognize one recorded sign and request warning, withdrawal, or a share without proving identity.
obligations: Refuse binding in the defeated champion's name
failure_modes: Letting personal standing replace the copy chain
Serving a rival branch for access

role_pressure_fields.summary: An outside mortuary witness whose case can hold an answer-roll copy beyond the branch registrar's sole custody.
obligations: Keep the route's material hazards distinct
failure_modes: Treating a complete copy as a complete person
Withholding evidence to protect the compact

known_context.text: Ves knows the bakehouse tally, current compact office list, her own route handoffs, household withdrawals, public branch marks, and what enters or leaves the scoring table.

beliefs.text: Ves believes exposure can be survived when a conspiracy's real leverage lies in necessary offices and separately held records.

misreads.text: Ves may overvalue a copy that cannot feed a household or reach a competent later forum.

must_not_know.text: Ves must not know the dead identity behind a sign, the Iron Shelter's full perception, Ash Hook's actual fracture evidence, or the rite's future outcome.

known_context.text: Nema knows Ninth Furnace's orders, branch copy, admitted petition token, named carriers she has stopped, and the marks placed in her case.

beliefs.text: Nema believes unlisted coordination near a divine route is both a security risk and a rival authority claim.

misreads.text: Nema may treat the branch that benefits from delay as the compact's owner without evidence of an agreement.

must_not_know.text: Nema must not know the full route list before it is exposed or infer divine intent from a clean docket.

known_context.text: Taru knows his household copy, the defeated champion's recorded sign, the silent shrine, and the recognized act he intends to request.

beliefs.text: Taru believes a warning or withdrawal request can preserve the old champion's claim without accepting a new binding in that champion's name.

misreads.text: Taru may hear split route knowledge as distrust of his claim rather than protection against seizure.

must_not_know.text: Taru must not treat a familiar gesture as proof that the champion survives complete or wants the same petition.

known_context.text: Melka knows the custody and contents of copies actually placed in her case and the signs she has authority to witness.

beliefs.text: Melka believes independent custody is useful only if she remains free to record evidence adverse to whoever paid her costs.

misreads.text: Melka may underestimate how the branch uses delay and access to punish households before a later hearing.

must_not_know.text: Melka must not identify a manifestation beyond the recorded sign and corroborating testimony.

author_only_boundaries.text: Projection, God Beast, thaumavore, oracle ecology, and timeline capture are backstage terms. Characters may speak of gods, routes, signs, shrines, feeding, branch pressure, and records but do not receive the author taxonomy.
The Ash-Below Compact is one Spoilers-tier authored local alliance. It does not settle native sect terminology, Jamnai-wide conspiracy practice, or universal appeal law.

The fixture may change which claims, copies, and relief stores reach the threshold. It must not choose the Ash-Halo Court's canonical outcome, identify the feeder, decide what the dead want, or resolve Ash Hook's missing inspection copy.
Individual character appearances, bakehouse dimensions, and the compact's current personnel are local authored detail, not universal Terjamna physiology or Jamnai architecture.
